name: SQL Query Correctness (Text-to-SQL / Execution Accuracy)
description: A natural-language question over a SQLite fixture, answered with a single read-only SELECT statement. Verified by actually executing sql_query against a fresh database built from schema_ddl + fixture_data and comparing the real result set to expected_result -- the Spider/BIRD 'execution accuracy' methodology, not a text/AST comparison against a reference query.
executionEnv: python3 (stdlib sqlite3 -- no separate database server)

fields.label: Task / question
fields.help: The natural-language question sql_query must answer over the fixture defined by schema_ddl + fixture_data.

fields.label: Schema (DDL)
fields.help: One or more CREATE TABLE statements defining the fixture. Executed via sqlite3 executescript() into a fresh database, before fixture_data. ATTACH/DETACH/PRAGMA are blocked as a sandbox-hygiene measure and are never needed here.

fields.label: Fixture data (INSERT statements)
fields.help: INSERT statements populating the tables declared in schema_ddl, executed via executescript() after schema_ddl. Use real, varied data -- the harness re-verifies that sql_query's result actually depends on this data (see the anti-hardcoding check) by re-running the same query against a generically mutated copy of it.

fields.label: SQL query
fields.help: A single, read-only SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT, including recursive CTEs) statement that answers task_description. No DDL/DML, no ATTACH/PRAGMA, no stacked ;-separated statements -- any of those are rejected before the query is ever executed, not merely disallowed by convention.

fields.label: Query category
fields.help: Forced diversity dimension for the dataset -- not read by the verifier itself.

fields.label: Expected result
fields.help: JSON array of row-arrays, in column-output order, e.g. [[1, "Ada", 36], [2, "Grace", 41]]. Column NAMES are never compared -- only cell values, by position -- matching Python's sqlite3 cursor.fetchall() shape and avoiding any requirement to alias computed/aggregate columns. Encode SQL NULL as JSON null. Encode SQLite's 0/1 boolean convention as a JSON number (0/1 preferred; JSON true/false is also accepted as a convenience). If sql_query contains ORDER BY, row order must match exactly; otherwise rows are compared as a multiset (order-insensitive) -- this exactly mirrors the BIRD/Spider text-to-SQL execution-accuracy methodology.
